summary: Discovery call to align on Lumenix's vector search roadmap, ops constraints, and tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private deployment for high-throughput similarity + rerank. Key themes: target qps and tail latency, embedding dim/quant choices, hybrid fanout vs single-store rerank, VPC and KMS requirements, and a 1-week benchmark pilot. Redwood AE+SE will provide cost scenarios and run benchmarks. Customer wants clear SLOs and an ops playbook for fallback routing.
topics: hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — im Alex, AE on Redwood Inference. we also have Priya and Diego from SE. can i get quick intros from the Lumenix side?
[00:12] Tom Reynolds: yeah Tom here, head of search. Maya is our infra lead, Samir is our CTO and Ellen on SRE. thanks for doing this.
[00:20] Alex Kim: great. high level, you sent over your doc about real-time recommendations and a rerank layer — we looked through it. goal for today is to understand your qps, latency targets, data residency and security needs so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:36] Maya Chen: cool. quick numbers: production traffic is about 5k qps for reads across our retail surface, but the rerank stage is applied to a smaller bucket — say 700 to 1,200 qps. peak bursts can spike up 2x. tail latency requirement for user-facing flows is 150ms P95 end-to-end, so we want the rerank step to be under 40ms ideally.
[01:02] Priya Shah: ok that's really helpful. when you say rerank under 40ms, is that single-stage rerank on the app tier, or are you doing fanout (embeddings + external VDB scoring + then rerank)?
[01:15] Tom Reynolds: we currently do a hybrid: initial recall from our vector DB (we use an in-house index with ANN), then an LLM reranker for top 10 results. we're exploring consolidating more in a single runtime to reduce network hops.
[01:29] Diego Morales: understood. a couple of things that drive latency: placement of the rerank model vs vector DB, network egress between Redis/ANN and model, and whether embeddings are precomputed or generated on the fly. also batching and KV cache hit rate matter.
[01:44] Maya Chen: embeddings are precomputed. size of the corpus is ~300M vectors, currently 512 dims but we're experimenting with 256 and 128 quantized versions to reduce storage and read latency.
[01:57] Alex Kim: 300M at 512 dims is sizable — are you sharded across multiple VDB nodes?
[02:03] Tom Reynolds: yes, it's sharded; we have fanout logic at query time that hits ~20 shards for full recall; topK then goes to rerank.
[02:11] Priya Shah: hitting 20 shards explains read amplification and tail variance. two common patterns we see: 1) keep the vector DB external and run lightweight rerank in Redwood (hosted/dedicated) with optimized network placement and KV caches; 2) co-locate a compact index on the same nodes as the model runtime (private/dedicated) to reduce fanout. both have tradeoffs on cost and operational complexity.
[02:34] Samir Patel: what's the delta on cost and latency between those?
[02:38] Priya Shah: rough ballpark — for your qps, a hosted approach with autoscaling and prefix caching can meet P95 40ms for rerank if we keep the model small (quantized 7-8bit) and you accept 1.5-2x egress overhead to your VDB. Dedicated gives you more predictable tail latency — fewer network hops if we colocate in the same VPC region or direct peering, but you pay for reserved capacity. Private (on-prem/VPC with customer-managed infra) reduces egress and increases control but needs extra setup and maintenance.
[03:07] Ellen Wu: on VPC, we have strict egress rules — we prefer private endpoints and aggressive firewall whitelisting; we also use a customer KMS.
[03:16] Alex Kim: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and VPC-only control planes. we can run the inference runtime in your VPC so traffic never leaves your network. that would also let you colocate the model near the VDB to eliminate cross-cloud hops.
[03:28] Tom Reynolds: how about quantization? you said 7-8bit — will that affect rerank quality? our business cares about relevance at the top-3 mostly.
[03:36] Diego Morales: quantization usually has modest impact on vector similarity for embeddings if you re-eval with samples. we recommend a two-track: keep full-precision vectors for freshness-critical cohorts or long-tail queries and use compact quantized indexes for the bulk. also we can do a hybrid rerank where the model sees full-precision vectors for the short list only (so less data to load).
[03:57] Maya Chen: interesting. storage for 300M x 512 at float32 is heavy. we're already planning to move to PQ + 8-bit hybrid to save cost. what's Redwood's approach to embedding dimensionality and serving options?
[04:11] Priya Shah: we expose options to host embeddings with the model runtime (embedding lookup cache) and also integrate with external VDBs. Redwood Optimize can recommend optimal dim/quant profiles per workload. operationally we suggest a small validation sweep: pick 10k representative queries, test 512/256/128 and PQ profiles, measure recall and downstream rerank delta.
[04:31] Tom Reynolds: can you run that sweep as part of the pilot?
[04:33] Priya Shah: yes — that's part of the benchmark package we run during the 1-week pilot. we'll need your sample queries and a small slice of index or a proxy dataset.
[04:42] Samir Patel: how do you handle KV cache invalidation and prefix caching? we saw cache thrashing issues before with bursty traffic.
[04:49] Diego Morales: Redwood runtime supports workload-aware batching and prefix caching with TTLs. for bursty traffic you'll want adaptive cache sizing and an LRU with hot-key pinning. we can instrument token-level metrics so you can see cache hit rates and token-econ.
[05:05] Ellen Wu: network question: if we do dedicated in our AWS account, do we have to open ports to Redwood control plane? we don't want management plane commands crossing our public net.
[05:14] Alex Kim: for Dedicated we offer a private peering option; the control plane uses a management channel but we can restrict control plane comms to a private transit VPC or use an air-gapped private deployment for Private customers. we'll share the architecture doc.
[05:28] Maya Chen: also SOC2 and audit logs — we need detailed audit trails for model versions, prompt inputs, and who triggered runs.
[05:36] Priya Shah: Redwood Console includes token-level cost traces and model-level audit logs; for Private we can stream logs to your SIEM and integrate with SSO/SAML for RBAC. we'll attach the SOC2 summary in the follow-up.
[05:47] Tom Reynolds: ok rough requirements recap from our side: keep rerank P95 under 40ms, support 700-1.2k rerank qps with 2x burst, 300M corpus, prefer 256 dims but test 128 for cost, strict VPC/KMS requirements, and audits.
[06:05] Alex Kim: that's a good summary. for architecture, we wanted to check your openness to a hybrid design: run lightweight candidate generation on your VDB, then send the top 50 to Redwood-hosted dedicated runtime for rerank with a hot-key cache. fallback policy would be to use a cheaper fallback model if capacity constrained. thoughts?
[06:22] Tom Reynolds: sounds reasonable. our main worry is tail latency when the VDB fanout is wide and nodes are hot. could Redwood help with shard routing or top-K pre-aggregation?
[06:31] Diego Morales: yes, we have a few approaches: 1) pre-aggregate shard-level topK at index time and route only to a subset at query time, 2) use query-side rerank with lower recall thresholds and use an async backfill for offline scoring, or 3) colocate a compact index in the runtime to avoid the 20-shard fanout. each reduces tail differently and has different cost/ops.
[06:53] Maya Chen: can you quantify tail improvement for colocating a compact index?
[06:58] Priya Shah: ballpark: eliminating a 20-shard fanout plus cross-AZ egress can cut tail variance dramatically — you might go from 120-200ms tail from the DB step to under 20-30ms for that step, leaving rerank as the main contributor. overall P95 could drop from 180ms to 60-80ms depending on model size and batching.
[07:20] Samir Patel: what's the model sizing profile for rerank? we plan to use a lightweight cross-encoder — around 350M parameters. if we quantize to 8-bit and use KV cache, what are the RAM/GPU footprints?
[07:31] Diego Morales: a 350M cross-encoder quantized to 8-bit typically fits on mid-range GPUs; runtime memory depends on sequence length and KV cache behavior. we can share a sizing guide. Dedicated nodes can host multiple replicas to support your qps and reduce instance counts with batching.
[07:46] Ellen Wu: one more operational question — how do you handle model rollouts and fallbacks? we need canarying and instant fallbacks to a cheaper model if a rollout causes regressions.
[07:55] Priya Shah: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, traffic splitting, and automatic fallback policies to a pinned model family. we also integrate eval sets so you can detect regression on key prompts.
[08:08] Tom Reynolds: good. let's talk about the benchmark — what do you need from us to run the 1-week throughput test?
[08:15] Priya Shah: we'll need: 1) a representative query trace (qps distribution and topk), 2) sample documents or a small slice of the index, 3) network constraints and VPC details for peering, and 4) your success criteria (latency, quality). Priya: can i get that from you, Maya?
[08:31] Maya Chen: yes i'll share the request. i want to make sure the benchmark uses our real query distribution not a synthetic uniform load.
[08:37] Diego Morales: we will run both hosted and dedicated profiles in the harness so you can compare cost and SLOs side-by-side. we'll also run a dim/quant sweep and measure top-3 accuracy delta.
[08:49] Tom Reynolds: pricing — ballpark numbers? we need to present to finance.
[08:54] Alex Kim: i'll prepare three scenarios: hosted on-demand with autoscaling, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly), and a private deployment estimate (one-time infra + monthly support). each will include recommended instance types, expected cost per 1M rerank calls, and approximate TCO over 12 months.
[09:10] Samir Patel: what about egress costs to our VDB for hosted?
[09:13] Alex Kim: for hosted, egress is on your side and depends on data transfer. we model egress into the TCO and can show sensitivity. dedicated in your account reduces egress. private eliminates public egress.
[09:23] Maya Chen: do you support conditional routing by query class? some queries are latency sensitive (homepage) others are async. we want to route by policy.
[09:31] Priya Shah: yes, Redwood Smart Routing supports per-route policies and SLO-based routing. you can pin critical routes to low-latency dedicated pools and route background jobs to cheaper clusters with higher latency SLOs.
[09:44] Tom Reynolds: any red flags we should be aware of?
[09:47] Diego Morales: initial friction is usually index integration and stable query trace collection for benchmarks. also getting private peering set up can take time. we recommend starting with a hosted pilot to get quick metrics, then move to dedicated once you've validated recall/quality.
[10:00] Ellen Wu: timeline — how quickly can you run the pilot?
[10:03] Priya Shah: once we have your sample data and IAM/network details, we can spin up the pilot in 3-5 business days. the 1-week run then gives us data to compare.
[10:13] Tom Reynolds: okay that works. who will be our point of contact?
[10:16] Alex Kim: Alex will own commercial, Priya will run the technical pilot, Diego will do sizing and Diego/Lina will handle post-sale CS.
[10:25] Samir Patel: procurement — we'd likely need a PoC agreement and an MSA later for dedicated. what's Redwood's typical procurement time?
[10:32] Alex Kim: enterprise procurement varies; for dedicated customers it's usually 4-8 weeks once legal signs off. we'll provide a standard PoC agreement for the pilot.
[10:40] Maya Chen: on the security doc — please include details on key rotation, log retention and where logs land.
[10:47] Priya Shah: will do. we'll attach SOC2 and KMS integration guides.
[10:52] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. i want to call out that our top-3 relevance needs to hold — if quantization drops top-3 too much, finance won't sign off. make sure the benchmark tracks top-3 MRR or NDCG.
[11:04] Diego Morales: absolutely — we'll include top-3 metrics and a significance test.
[11:09] Alex Kim: ok let's recap action items and next steps. Alex to send hosting/pricing scenarios, Priya to set up the benchmark, Maya to send traces and infra constraints, Ellen to share firewall rules, Samir to confirm procurement cadence. we'll reconvene after the benchmark.
[11:24] Tom Reynolds: thanks all. any final quick notes?
[11:27] Ellen Wu: please include explicit IP ranges and ports in the doc.
[11:30] Alex Kim: noted. we'll email the packet today and target a follow-up within 10 days. thanks everyone.
[11:36] (call ends)
notes: References: shared deck link (redwood-hosting-roadmap.pdf), benchmark template (redwood-benchmark-harness.xlsx). Customer emphasized top-3 quality and strict VPC/KMS needs. Pilot cadence: 3-5 days prep + 1 week run. Next meeting to review benchmark results.
